question_text: Where does the formation of urea take place in our body?
explanation: Urea formation occurs in the liver through the urea cycle (or ornithine cycle). It removes toxic ammonia produced from protein metabolism. The urea is transported to the kidneys for excretion through urine. This helps maintain nitrogen balance in the body. Hence, the correct answer is liver.
source: brain and nervous system - science.pdf p. 16

question_text: Which of these is an excretory organ of the human body?
explanation: Skin has a role in excretion by producing sweat. Sweating eliminates excess salts, water, and urea. The heart pumps blood through an artery network; the brain is the central organ of the nervous system; the spinal cord makes up the central nervous system. Hence, the correct answer is skin.
source: brain and nervous system - science.pdf p. 17
